headline: Approved consent agenda, including $16,863.40 in tax refunds and Electric and Sewer budget changes.
summary: Residents raised crosswalk signs, a sidewalk project, and Parade Ground driveway access. The Mayor reported $35,966,647.35 in expenditures to date for the new Police Department. The Mayor also said Golden Fox Theatre grant funds have not been processed because conditions are missing.
decisions: Approved consent agenda items 3a through 3k by voice vote, with all councilors present voting.

decision_evidence.quote: MOTION WAS MADE TO approve Consent items 3a – 3k. ... THERE WAS A VOICE VOTE. ALL COUNCILORS PRESENT VOTED. MOTION: PASSED

TOWN OF WALLINGFORD, CONNECTICUT 
TOWN COUNCIL MEETING 
Robert F. Parisi Council Chambers  
November 24, 2026 
6:30 P.M. 
RECORD OF VOTES AND MINUTES 
 
The Town Council Meeting on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, was called to order at 6:35pm. The Pledge of 
Allegiance was said. Councilors in attendance were Samuel Carmody, Thomas Laffin, Jesse Reynolds, Bryan 
Rivard, Melanie Rossacci, Christina Tatta and Chairman Vincent F. Testa, Jr. Mayor Vincent Cervoni, Town 
Attorney Geoffrey Einhorn, Comptroller Tim Sena and Acting Town Clerk, Leanna Gnazzo were also present. 
 
1. Pledge of Allegiance   
 
2. Roll Call  
 
 Remarks from the Chair  
 
3. Consent Agenda

Marshall for Public Education needs and consider and approve Appropriation of funds in the 
amount of $250 to Revenue Account-Donations, Acct. #2502002-47152 and to Expense 
Account-Fire Dept. Program Expenditures, Acct. #25020150-58830-10160 – Fire Dept.   
   
3c. Acceptance of donations for youth recreation enrollment and consider and approve 
Appropriation of funds in the amount of $331 to Revenue, Acct. #2134002-47152 and to 
Expenditures, Acct. #21340100-58830 – Youth and Social Services Dept.   
  
3d. Consider and approve FY 2026-2027 budget amendment and Appropriation of funds in the 
amount of $36,115 from Retained Earnings, Acct. #N/A to Pumping Plant – Electric Pumping 
Equip., Acct. #46300325 – Sewer Div. 
 
3e. Consider and approve FY 2026-2027 budget amendment and Appropriation of funds in the 
amount of $273,800 from Retained Earnings, Acct. #N/A to Treatment Plant Equipment,  
 Acct. #46300332 – Sewer Div.

MOTION WAS MADE TO approve Consent items 3a – 3k. 
 
MADE BY:  CARMODY 
SECONDED BY: REYNOLDS 
 
THERE WAS A VOICE VOTE. ALL COUNCILORS PRESENT VOTED.  
MOTION: PASSED 
 
 
  4. Items Removed from the Consent Agenda 
 
 
 5. PUBLIC QUESTION & ANSWER PERIOD 
 
Larry Kellogg addressed the Council regarding crosswalk signage. He reported that he has been exploring 
opportunities to obtain donations from local businesses to fund the purchase of approximately 50 signs to be 
installed at public school crosswalks. Chairman Testa expressed support for the project and stated that he would 
consult with the appropriate departments to determine what would be needed to move the project forward. 
 
Sheila Tierney requested an update on the sidewalk project. Chairman Testa stated that the matter would be 
addressed at the December 8, 2026 meeting, as certain department heads were unavailable due to the holiday 
week.
Wallingford, Connecticut

3
 
Ms. Tierney also raised concerns regarding public access to the Parade Ground driveway and the need for 
signage to prevent unauthorized traffic. The Mayor clarified that the Parade Ground driveway is open to the 
public and is not restricted. It may be used to access the Town Hall parking lot and by residents of 35 South 
Main Street and 41 South Main Street. 
 
Jason Michael inquired about the Town Council Rules and Procedures regarding requests for information from 
department heads. The Mayor emphasized the importance of keeping questions focused on agenda items so that 
department heads can provide informed and relevant responses. 
 
Mr. Michael also asked about the final cost of the new Police Department. The Mayor reported that 
expenditures to date total $35,966,647.35. 
 
Bill Comerford inquired about the Pragemann Park Pavilion and whether the department head and the matter 
would be placed on a future agenda. Chairman Testa confirmed that the item would be included on the 
December 8, 2026 meeting agenda. 
 
Mr. Comerford also asked the Mayor about correspondence he had received concerning 60 Prince Street. The 
Mayor stated that he had received a letter from the Director of Public Works indicating that an investigation had 
been conducted and that no evidence was found to support the presence of contamination. 
 
 6. Discussion of Old Business – Chairman Testa 
            (a) Golden Fox Theatre  
 
Chairman Testa asked for an update on this issue of disbursement of grant funds.  He stated that if there is no 
movement towards resolution, it cannot continue to be put on the agenda.  He noted that it can still be raised at 
future meetings during Public Question and Answer.  Mayor responded that the funds have not been processed 
due to missing conditions.  He stated that he had offered to meet with Mr. Michael to assist him in completing 
his budget.  Mr. Michaels feels that additional conditions continue to be added, and he does not feel he should 
be required to provide further documentation.  He feels the Council approved his application, and the funds 
should be disbursed. 
 
7.        Executive Session pursuant to Connecticut General Statures §1-200(6)(D) and §1-225(f) for discussion    
           with respect to the purchase of property – Law Dept.  
 
MOTION WAS MADE TO enter Executive Session pursuant to CGS Sections 1-225(f) and 1-200(6)(C) 
for discussion with respect to the purchase of property at 7:20 PM. 
 
MADE BY: CARMODY  
SECONDED BY: REYNOLDS 
 
THERE WAS A VOICE VOTE. ALL COUNCILORS PRESENT VOTED AYE.  
MOTION: PASSED
